label: EVIDENCE
text: The source dataset (Petretto et al., 2018) has ab initio full phonon dispersions and vibrational densities of states for 1521 semiconductor compounds. They were calculated with density functional perturbation theory in the harmonic approximation and checked against experimental data. So the oracle values are harmonic DFPT phonon DOS for semiconductors, not measured spectra.

label: EVIDENCE
text: Choudhary et al. (2020) computed Gamma-point phonons for 5015 non-metallic materials (JARVIS-DFT) with high-throughput DFPT. They looked at chemistry, symmetry, dimensionality and geometry as features that explain variation in the data, and built regression models for the highest infrared frequency that they report as high-accuracy. Caveat: the target is the highest IR-active Gamma-point mode, not the last peak of the full phonon DOS, and the abstract does not separate how much composition versus structure contributes.

label: EVIDENCE
text: Lookman et al. (2019) review active learning in materials science. It works iteratively: a surrogate model makes predictions with uncertainties, and a utility function uses them to choose which unexplored candidates to evaluate next. The review discusses several utility functions applied in both computational and experimental materials work.

label: EVIDENCE
text: Rohr et al. (2020) benchmark sequential learning on datasets where every candidate's performance is known (fully enumerated metal-oxide spaces). They score performance against separate research goals: finding any good material, finding all good materials, and getting an accurate predictive model. This supports judging a screening campaign by a fully-known-pool metric such as top-k recall, kept separate from model accuracy. The excerpt does not report which algorithm won.

label: EVIDENCE
text: A 2026 preprint states that conventional Bayesian optimization can become inefficient as discrete candidate spaces grow, often evaluating low-value regions before reaching informative ones under limited budgets. It reports that active-learning-guided narrowing of the search space improved early convergence in its test cases: COF gas separation and pressure-vessel design. Not peer reviewed, and not about phonons.

label: EVIDENCE
text: A 2025 preprint on active correlation clustering treats cold start (no initial labels) as a specific challenge for active learning. It proposes a coverage-aware method that encourages diversity early in the process, and reports that it works well in synthetic and real experiments. This is evidence from outside materials science that early diversity helps under cold start; it does not test materials screening.

label: EVIDENCE
text: A 2023 dissertation on active learning with random forests shows that random forests are stable under mild conditions. That stability gives coverage guarantees for prediction intervals built from out-of-bag error. It also reports that a bias-oriented and a variance-oriented random-forest active learning method complement each other. This bears on how trustworthy random-forest uncertainty is as an input to an acquisition function such as expected improvement.

label: UNCERTAINTY
text:
What the literature found does NOT establish:
(1) No source returned here directly says that light atoms or stiff bonds raise the highest phonon frequencies. The search on bond stiffness and atomic mass gave only off-target results. Treat the light-element / stiff-bond heuristic as textbook-level INFERENCE until it is cited.
(2) No source compares RF+EI against random screening on this dataset or on the last-phonon-DOS-peak target, and none gives an expected effect size for top-5% recall.
(3) No source measures how much crystal structure adds beyond composition for the phonon DOS peak frequency. Choudhary 2020 (ev-002) uses both kinds of feature but does not split their contributions in the abstract, and its target is a different one: the highest IR-active Gamma-point mode.
(4) The cold-start and early-diversity evidence (ev-006) and the BO-inefficiency claim (ev-005) come from preprints outside materials or outside phonons. How far they carry over is unknown.
(5) The excerpts do not show how well random-forest uncertainty is calibrated in the extrapolative top tail, which is where expected improvement acts.
(6) No source shows that LLM-designed or 'evidence-informed' campaigns beat standard BO.
(7) The pool characteristics (size, distribution of the target, overlap with Petretto's 1521 compounds) must come from the pool summary, not from the literature. Harmonic DFPT values carry their own systematic error relative to experiment (ev-001).

text:
CRITIQUE OF h-001 (structure adds signal).
(1) THE DECISION RULE IS TOO WEAK STATISTICALLY. +0.03 recall is 2 of 63 hits, and recall moves in steps of 1/63 ≈ 0.016, so the threshold is only two steps above zero. Under a true null (paired difference symmetric around 0), P(≥7/10 positive seeds) = 176/1024 ≈ 0.17. Ties (difference exactly 0) are likely at this granularity and the rule does not say how to count them. With an assumed paired SD of 0.04–0.06 across seeds (seed variance is dominated by the cold-start draw, see 4), a paired t-test with n=10 has roughly 30–50% power to detect a true +0.03. The test is underpowered and prone to false positives at the same time. A confirmatory 'win' at 10 seeds is weak evidence, and a 'loss' is close to uninformative.
(2) DILUTION AND RF max_features CONFOUND. Structure is 4 of 127 columns. If the RF uses max_features='sqrt' (≈11 per split), a given split sees at least one structure column only about 30% of the time. If it uses 1.0 (the sklearn regressor default), dilution mostly disappears. A null result could therefore reflect a hyperparameter, not a lack of information. Also, the composition_structure arm changes the RF's tree diversity and so its variance estimate, which changes EI's exploration behaviour. Any Δ mixes 'better mean prediction' with 'different uncertainty', so the hypothesis cannot attribute a win to structural information.
(3) REDUNDANCY. Magpie includes element-wise GSvolume_pa and mass statistics, and density ≈ mass/volume. 'volume per atom' and 'density' are partly predictable from composition. n_sites is a complexity/cell-size proxy that may track dataset provenance (Materials Project prototype families) rather than physics. A structure 'win' could come only from n_sites acting as a family identifier.
(4) COLD START AND SEED VARIANCE. With 63/1265 top-5% and 20 random initial points, P(zero top-5% hits in the initial set) ≈ 0.95^20 ≈ 0.36. About a third of seeds start blind to the target tail, and this probably explains more variance than the feature set does. Both arms must share the identical initial 20 per seed (true pairing). If they do not, the comparison is invalid.
(5) POOL CENSORING AND RETROSPECTIVE ORACLE. The pool is 1265 of Petretto's 1521 (ev-001). If removed entries are dynamically unstable or failed calculations (imaginary modes), the remaining pool is cleaner and smoother than a real prospective screen, and structure features (packing, volume) may correlate with exactly the instability that was filtered out. The effect does not transfer to unfiltered pools. The structures are also DFT-relaxed with the same functional as the oracle. That is mild information leakage: a prospective screen would use unrelaxed or database structures.
(6) POLYMORPHS. If the pool contains duplicate formulas (polymorphs), composition-only features cannot tell them apart, and labelling one gives the other nearly for free. Count duplicate formulas and report Δ with and without them.
(7) MODEL ACCURACY ≠ DISCOVERY. Borg et al. 2023 (d2dd00113f) show that regression error metrics are decoupled from sequential-learning discovery performance. An offline CV gain from structure features must NOT be cited as support.
FALSIFICATION (sharpened): h-001 is falsified if the 95% paired bootstrap (or t) CI on Δ = recall(comp+struct) − recall(comp) at budget 200 includes 0, OR the mean Δ < +0.03, OR wins (ties excluded and reported separately) < 8/10. It is also falsified if Δ disappears under the permuted-structure control below (≥50% of Δ retained by the permuted arm means no structural information effect).
REQUIRED CONTROLS / CHANGES: (a) Add a permuted-structure arm: same 127 columns with the 4 structure columns shuffled across rows. This controls for column count and RF variance artefacts. (b) Fix and report RF max_features, and preferably run the comparison at max_features=1.0 and 'sqrt'. Declare which is primary BEFORE running. (c) Raise to ≥20 seeds (30 preferred). The threshold of 7/10 corresponds to ~0.17 false-positive rate, so use a Wilcoxon signed-rank p<0.05 one-sided plus mean Δ ≥ 0.03. (d) Add the area under the recall-vs-calls curve (AUC over 0..200) as the preregistered secondary instead of censored calls-to-50%, which is low-power. (e) Report Δ stratified by number of top-5% hits in the initial 20 (0 vs ≥1). (f) State explicitly whether the 20 initial points are inside the 200 budget and whether initial hits count toward recall. This must be identical across arms.

text:
CRITIQUE OF h-002 (UCB / family-diverse batches beat EI by ≥ +0.05).
(1) THE ELEMENT_FAMILY DIVERSITY CONSTRAINT IS PROBABLY A NO-OP. h-002 itself states 1082 families in 1265 compounds, with the largest family having 6 members. A 'one per family' batch rule therefore almost never binds, and a 10-point EI batch will rarely contain two members of the same family by chance. The proposed mechanism (EI collapsing onto chemically similar compounds) cannot be counteracted by a constraint at this granularity. Real chemical mode collapse happens at a coarser level, e.g. 'contains B/C/N/O/H' or the anion class. Before running, compute how often B_baseline_ei batches violate the family constraint. If that is <5% of batches, the diversity arm is the baseline under another name and must be dropped or redefined at a coarser level (e.g. anion or light-element group, or k-means clusters in feature space).
(2) MULTIPLE COMPARISONS AND TUNING ON THE TEST. 'UCB with kappa in 1–3, and/or diversity' is a family of arms. If several kappa values × {diversity on/off} are run on the same 10 seeds and the best one is compared to baseline, the max-of-k selection inflates the expected Δ. With 4–6 arms and seed SD ≈ 0.05, a spurious +0.03–0.05 is plausible from selection alone. The hypothesis does not name a single confirmatory arm. That is a forking-paths problem. Also, an LLM 'agent' designing the strategy may have prior knowledge of this public dataset (Petretto 2018) or of phonon physics (prioritise light elements). If the agent's choices encode memorised label structure, that is leakage through priors, not acquisition merit.
(3) CEILING. Budget 200 is ~16% of the pool. If B_baseline_ei already reaches recall ≥0.85, the +0.05 margin requires ≥3 of the remaining ≤9 hits, and the test becomes about ceiling compression, not strategy. Preregister: if mean baseline recall > 0.85, use recall AUC over the budget (or recall at budget 100) as primary, not recall@200.
(4) BASELINE DEFINITION DRIVES THE RESULT. How is a batch of 10 chosen under EI: top-10 EI scores (no fantasisation / Kriging believer / local penalisation)? Naive top-q EI is a weak baseline that any diversity heuristic will beat. EI's xi parameter and the RF variance estimator (tree spread vs jackknife) are also unstated. UCB κ is on the RF tree-SD scale, and RF tree SD is often near zero for points near training data and badly calibrated in the extrapolative tail (ev-gaps item 5), so κ=1–3 may have effectively the same ranking as EI or as pure-mean. A UCB 'win' may reflect that the RF variance is badly scaled, not that exploration is good.
(5) COLD START. P(no top-5% in initial 20) ≈ 0.36. Exploration-heavy arms will look best precisely in those seeds and may lose in the others. With 10 seeds the mix of the two regimes is random (expected ~3.6 blind seeds, SD ~1.5), so the aggregate Δ depends on the draw. Stratify by initial-hit count.
(6) POOL CENSORING AND RETROSPECTIVE ORACLE. The cleaned pool has no failed or unstable calculations, so wasted exploration costs nothing beyond a call. In a prospective campaign, exploration into unusual chemistries hits instability and convergence failures more often. A retrospective win for exploration overstates the prospective value.
(7) LITERATURE CUTS AGAINST LARGE GAINS. Liang et al. 2021 (npj Comput Mater) find RF and anisotropic GP comparable in BO across five experimental domains, with modest acquisition-function differences. The 2026 BO benchmark (zkvt6687) finds EI consistently strong and used only 5 seeds. Supporting evidence for h-002 (ev-005, ev-006) is preprint-only and off-domain. The prior of 0.35 is, if anything, generous for a ≥+0.05 effect.
FALSIFICATION (sharpened): name ONE confirmatory arm before running (recommended: UCB κ=2 on tree-SD, no diversity; OR coarse-family diversity with EI, not both). h-002 is falsified if, for that arm vs B_baseline_ei on matched seeds and identical initial sets, mean Δrecall@budget < +0.05, OR the 95% paired CI lower bound ≤ 0, OR wins < 8/10 (ties reported). If >1 arm is tested confirmatorily, apply Holm correction across arms. A kappa sweep must be done on separate tuning seeds (e.g. seeds 100–109) and confirmed on fresh seeds (0–19). Any arm selected after seeing results on the confirmation seeds is exploratory only.
REQUIRED CONTROLS: (a) a random-batch arm and a pure-exploitation arm (κ=0 / posterior mean). If κ=0 ≈ EI ≈ UCB, the acquisition axis is not where the signal is. (b) A family-constraint binding-rate diagnostic. (c) A batch-EI baseline with a penalty for redundancy (e.g. local penalisation or a Kriging believer), so the diversity arm is not beating a strawman. (d) ≥20 confirmation seeds.

text:
CRITIQUE OF h-003 (null: fixed RF+EI captures nearly all gain).
(1) ABSENCE OF EVIDENCE IS BEING SCORED AS EVIDENCE OF ABSENCE. Criterion (ii), 'Δ < 0.05 and ≤6/10 positive seeds', is satisfied by ANY underpowered experiment. With 10 seeds and paired SD ≈ 0.05, the 95% CI on Δ is roughly ±0.036 around the observed mean. A true +0.04 effect would 'confirm the null' most of the time. As written, h-003 is nearly unfalsifiable by a noisy run and will be 'supported' by default. It must be framed as an EQUIVALENCE claim: TOST with margin ±0.05, i.e. the 90% paired CI on Δ (best agent arm − baseline) lies entirely within (−0.05, +0.05). If the CI is wider than the margin, the verdict is INCONCLUSIVE, not 'null supported'.
(2) 'BEST AGENT ARM' SELECTION CUTS BOTH WAYS. Picking the max over several arms biases Δ upward, against h-003, which is conservative for the null. But if the agent explores few arms or weak ones, the null is trivially supported. Preregister the full set of agent arms that count. 'Nearly all the gain' must be relative to a stated upper reference, e.g. an oracle-greedy or a long-budget arm. Otherwise 'all available gain' is undefined.
(3) RANDOM BASELINE ARITHMETIC DEPENDS ON THE UNRESOLVED BUDGET ACCOUNTING. If the 20 initial points are inside the 200: E[recall_random] = 200/1265 ≈ 0.158 → the 2× bar is 0.316. If they are outside: 220/1265 ≈ 0.174 → the bar is 0.348. Fix this before running. Also, '~63' top-5% must be an exact integer with a stated tie rule at the threshold. Run an empirical random arm (same seeds) rather than relying on the analytic expectation, because random hits follow a hypergeometric distribution with SD ≈ 3 hits (≈0.045 recall).
(4) THE 2× BAR IS LOW AND UNINFORMATIVE. Model-guided search on a smooth, composition-dominated target in a clean pool will almost surely clear 2× random (e.g. recall ≥0.32). Part (i) is near-certain and adds no evidential weight. If you want it to discriminate, raise it (e.g. ≥3× random, or recall ≥0.5) and preregister it.
(5) RETROSPECTIVE ORACLE AND POOL CENSORING INFLATE THE BASELINE. Precomputed noiseless labels and the removal of 256 unstable or failed entries (1265 of 1521, ev-001) make the landscape smoother than reality. That favours exploitative EI and makes a null more likely here than in a prospective campaign. A null result is valid only for this cleaned retrospective pool. Do not generalise it to 'agentic design is unnecessary'.
(6) CHEMICAL-FAMILY MODE COLLAPSE CAN MASQUERADE AS SUCCESS. If the top 5% is concentrated in a few light-element chemistries (B, C, N, O, H, Be compounds), EI can reach high recall by mining one region. Equal recall across arms would then reflect the target's structure, not EI's adequacy. Report the chemical composition of the top-5% set (anion and light-element group counts) and the distinct-group coverage of hits per arm.
(7) THE CALLS-TO-50% CRITERION IS FRAGILE. It is censored at 200, quantised to batches of 10, and medians over 10 seeds are unstable. 'Within 10 calls' is exactly one batch, so it holds by quantisation in most comparisons. Replace it with recall AUC over the budget plus an equivalence margin.
(8) h-003 IS NOT THE EXACT COMPLEMENT OF h-002. h-002 fails if Δ < 0.05 OR wins < 7. h-003 holds if Δ < 0.05 AND wins ≤ 6. An outcome of Δ = 0.06 with 6/10 wins falsifies both, and Δ = 0.03 with 8/10 wins falsifies h-002 without supporting h-003. Define a three-way verdict ahead of time: h-002 supported / equivalence (h-003) supported / inconclusive.
FALSIFICATION (sharpened): h-003 is falsified if the preregistered best agent arm's paired 90% CI on Δrecall@budget has a lower bound > 0 AND mean Δ ≥ 0.05 (i.e. h-002 succeeds), OR if B_baseline_ei mean recall < 2× the EMPIRICAL random arm mean on the same seeds. h-003 is SUPPORTED only if the TOST shows equivalence within ±0.05 (requires ≥20, realistically ~30 seeds at SD 0.05). Otherwise the verdict is INCONCLUSIVE and must be reported as such.

text:
DECISION dec-001 on prereg-001 (run-prereg-001 / result-prereg-001). All numbers come from the stored results. Every verdict below is flagged ACCOUNTING UNVERIFIED and CEILING-COMPRESSED.

0. Gate checks.
- Pairing. The harness asserts the identical initial 20 per seed "by construction" and gives one hash per seed. There is no per-arm hash, so the check is ASSERTED, NOT INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED. The protocol-failure rule ("Pairing check fails ...") did not fire, because there is no evidence of failure. If later verification shows a mismatch, every paired verdict below is void.
- Accounting. The prereg says: "If the harness does not report them, flag every result as 'accounting unverified'". The harness did not report two things: the tie rule at the 95th-percentile cutoff, and whether the initial hits count toward recall. So that flag applies. The harness did report n_top = 63, and each seed made 220 oracle calls (initial 20 on top of the budget of 200). Empirical random recall was 0.176 against an analytic 0.174 under the "outside" accounting. That agreement suggests, but does not prove, that the initial hits are counted toward recall.

1. Primary, C_crucible vs B_baseline_ei. Mean delta recall +0.0317, 95% CI [0.0238, 0.0397], wins 10/0/0.
- RULE FIRED: "95% CI lower bound > 0 but mean delta < 0.05 or wins < 8/10 -> Statistically positive but below the preregistered practical margin: h-002 NOT supported at its threshold. h-003 is supported only if the TOST equivalence rule also passes."
- TOST check. The 90% CI is [0.0254, 0.0381], entirely inside (-0.05, +0.05), so equivalence passes. The equivalence rule's condition is also literally met: "C equivalent to B: 90% bootstrap CI on delta lies entirely within (-0.05, +0.05) -> h-003 equivalence SUPPORTED for this cleaned retrospective pool only; h-002 FALSIFIED. Do not generalise to 'agent design is unnecessary'".
- Formal verdict as written: h-002 not supported at its margin, and FALSIFIED under the equivalence rule. h-003 equivalence supported, limited to this pool.

2. Ceiling.
- RULE FIRED: "B_baseline_ei mean recall > 0.85 (ceiling) -> Report the primary verdict but flag it as ceiling-compressed. Recall AUC ... may NOT be used to overturn the primary verdict." B = 0.956.
- The AUC delta of +0.0327 (95% CI [0.0194, 0.0456], 9/1) points the same way. It is interpretive only.

3. SURPRISE that reopens an assumption. With B at 0.956, the largest possible gain in mean recall was 1 - 0.956 = 0.044. That is below the +0.05 practical margin. Under this protocol, h-002's success criterion was unreachable before the run began. The equivalence margin is also no longer informative: a delta that is positive on 10/10 seeds and lifts C to 0.987 (5 of 10 seeds reach recall 1.0) is labelled "equivalent".
- So the rules were applied exactly as written, but the result mostly shows that the margin was set without checking the baseline's headroom. It does not show that UCB kappa=2 makes no difference.
- The lab's actual belief is narrower: on this pool, UCB kappa=2 gives a small, consistent gain in recall over RF+EI (about +0.03, 2 of the 63 targets per seed). Whether that is practically meaningful cannot be judged at this budget.
- C also reached 50% recall at a median of 90 calls against B's 100 (ratio 1.111). The effect is small.

4. Structure vs composition, B_baseline_ei minus B_ablation_composition_only. Delta recall +0.0111, 95% CI [-0.0032, 0.0222], 8/1/1. Delta AUC -0.0134, 95% CI [-0.042, 0.014], 3/7.
- RULE FIRED: "Structure vs composition, null or small: 95% CI on delta_s includes 0 OR mean < 0.03 OR wins < 8/10 -> h-001 NOT supported. Do not conclude that structure carries no information: dilution (4 of 127 columns) and the undeclared max_features are unresolved confounds."
- The negative rule did not fire, because the upper bound 0.0222 > 0.
- The recall and AUC deltas point in opposite directions, which is consistent with no detectable feature-set effect.

5. Model-guided premise. B is 0.956, far above 2 x 0.176 for A_random, so the falsification condition for h-003 part (i) did NOT fire. C vs A_random gives +0.811, 95% CI [0.7825, 0.8381], 10/10.
- RULE FIRED: "C vs A_random: 95% CI on paired (C minus A) has lower bound > 0 -> The agent arm beats random; report the effect size." This does not change the primary verdict.

6. Secondaries.
- By how many top-5% hits the initial set contained, the C-B delta is 0.0349 with zero initial hits (n=5) and 0.0286 with one or more (n=5). There is no sign that the result depends on a lucky start, though n is small.
- Diversity (declared deviation, a distinct element-set count rather than the preregistered anion / light-element groups): A 11.0, B 57.2, ablation 56.5, C 59.2. There is no mode collapse. These counts track the number of hits almost one-to-one, so this proxy has little power to detect collapse.

7. Updated beliefs (INFERENCE; the h-001/h-002/h-003 entry texts and prior confidences were not re-read in full this session, so these are absolute levels, not calibrated updates).
- h-001 (structure adds value): 0.25.
- h-002 (more exploration helps): 0.35. It fails its own margin and is formally falsified by the equivalence rule, but the direction is consistent and the margin was unreachable.
- h-003 (fixed RF+EI is sufficient / equivalent): 0.55. Equivalence passes formally and part (i) holds, but C beat B on every seed.
- Uncertainty is high. There are only 10 seeds, the accounting is unverified, and the ceiling compresses every recall contrast.

8. Next experiment, proposed; a human must approve it. Preregister a ceiling-free replication of C (UCB kappa=2) vs B (EI) with at least 20 fresh seeds, not seeds 0-9.
- Choose the primary endpoint so that B has real headroom: recall at an earlier checkpoint on the same curve, or a smaller budget / stricter top fraction if the harness allows it.
- Set the practical margin as a fraction of B's measured headroom, and check before running that it is reachable.
- Keep the arms identical otherwise.
- Require the harness to log the initial-set hash per arm, the tie rule and the recall accounting.
- Add the shuffled-structure control and a declared max_features if the harness gains them.

9. Validation still needed before real-world use. This was a retrospective, noiseless replay of precomputed DFPT labels on a cleaned subset (1265 of 1521). Real-world use would need:
- a prospective or held-out-pool test with real calculation cost and failures;
- a check that the RF uncertainty in the top tail is calibrated;
- a check on duplicate-polymorph leakage;
- replication on a second phonon-property dataset.
None of this licenses the claim "agent design is unnecessary" or "agent design is superior" outside this pool.

DECISION dec-002 on prereg-002 (run-prereg-002 / result-prereg-002). I checked the runner's summary against get_results(run-prereg-002) and the ledger, and every quoted number matches. 30 seeds (100-129), budget 100 plus the initial 20 (120 oracle calls per seed), n_top 63. Only the decision rules preregistered in prereg-002 are applied, with 95% CIs for superiority and inferiority and the 90% CI for TOST, as prereg-002 specifies.

0. Gate checks
- Pairing: pairing_check.verified = True, with per-arm initial-set hashes. The protocol-failure rule did NOT fire. This settles the "asserted, not verified" issue from dec-001.
- Ceiling: B_baseline_ei is 0.691, below 0.85, so the ceiling rule did NOT fire. The in-run guard (B > 0.75) also did not fire.
- Accounting: appr-prereg-002 confirms that oracle-call counts include the initial 20. The empirical random recall (0.091) matches the analytic expectation (0.0949), which is consistent with initial hits counting toward recall. The top-set tie rule is still not reported. Under the prereg's own rule ("If any is missing, flag every result 'accounting unverified'"), the flag stays on, but only for the tie rule.

1. Primary result: C_crucible vs B_baseline_ei
- Mean delta recall: +0.0296. 95% CI [-0.0042, 0.0608]. 90% CI [0.0016, 0.0561]. W/L/T 17/9/4, so C won 17/26 = 0.654 of non-tied seeds, below 2/3.
- Superiority (95% LB > 0): does not fire, because the lower bound is -0.0042.
- Positive-below-margin: does not fire, because it needs 95% LB > 0.
- Equivalence: does not fire. The 90% CI upper bound of 0.0561 exceeds +0.05.
- Inferiority: does not fire, because the 95% upper bound is 0.0608 > 0.
- RULE FIRED: "None of the above (95% CI includes 0 and the 90% CI extends beyond +/-0.05) -> INCONCLUSIVE for h-002 and h-003 even with 30 seeds. Report the CI width; this is not evidence for the null."
- CI widths: 95% 0.0650, 90% 0.0545. TOST failed by 0.0061 on the upper side.
- Secondary: AUC C-B is +0.0055, 95% CI [-0.0115, 0.0212], 21/9. Median calls to 50% recall is 90 for both arms (ratio 1.0).

2. Structure vs composition: B_baseline_ei minus B_ablation_composition_only
- delta_s +0.0164, 95% CI [-0.0206, 0.0561], 90% CI [-0.0153, 0.0497], W/L/T 18/11/1 (18/29 = 0.62 < 2/3). AUC delta -0.0012, 95% CI [-0.0248, 0.0254], 15/15.
- RULE FIRED: "Structure vs composition, null or small: 95% CI on delta_s includes 0 OR mean < 0.03 OR wins < 2/3 -> h-001 NOT supported." The 90% CI is not inside +/-0.03, so the "no detectable structure benefit even with headroom" statement is NOT licensed.
- The negative rule did not fire (upper bound 0.0561 > 0). Dilution (4 of 127 columns) remains a confound.

3. Other rules
- h-003 part (i): B 0.691 is not below 2 x 0.091 = 0.182, so the falsification rule did NOT fire. Model guidance is far better than random.
- RULE FIRED: "C vs A_random: 95% CI on paired (C - A) has lower bound > 0 -> Report that the agent arm beats random." C-A is +0.630, 95% CI [0.5905, 0.6683], 30/0/0. This is secondary and does not change the primary verdict.

4. Comparison with dec-001
- The point estimate replicates almost exactly on independent seeds: +0.0296 now vs +0.0317 at budget 200.
- Consistency does not replicate: 10/10 wins before, 17/9/4 now. The 95% CI now includes 0.
- dec-001's TOST equivalence (90% CI [0.0254, 0.0381]) does not hold here. The 90% upper bound of 0.0561 crosses the margin.
- The early-speed signal also does not replicate: calls-to-50% ratio 1.111 before vs 1.0 now, and the AUC gain is +0.0327 before vs +0.0055 now with a CI spanning 0.
- Net: this run WEAKENS dec-001 in both directions. It weakens the belief in a small but consistent C advantage, and it does not confirm dec-001's ceiling-compressed h-003 equivalence. It does not overturn either; it leaves them unresolved. The h-001 "not supported" verdict is CONFIRMED a second time.

5. Surprises that reopen assumptions
(a) Headroom was over-estimated. prereg-002 expected B at about 0.50, but B reached 0.691 (median calls to 50% recall was 90 on these seeds vs 100 before). Realised headroom is 0.309, so the 0.05 margin is about 16% of headroom, not the planned 10%. This reopens the assumption that a single median calls-to-50% figure is a reliable proxy for the recall curve. Future margins should come from stored per-seed recall values, which get_results now provides.
(b) Seed-to-seed heterogeneity is large. Per-seed C-B deltas range from -0.190 to +0.206. That is why 30 seeds could not resolve a delta of about 0.03.
(c) The stratified deltas reverse the prereg-001 pattern. Seeds with 0 initial top hits (n=9) give +0.0071; seeds with 1 or more (n=21) give +0.0393. In prereg-001 it was 0.0349 vs 0.0286, with n=5 each. Any benefit of UCB kappa=2 may depend on the starting set. This only generates a hypothesis; the n is small and it was not a primary test.
(d) The diversity proxy (declared deviation: distinct element sets, not the preregistered anion / light-element groups) gives C 42.7, B 40.8, ablation 39.57, A 5.73. It again tracks the hit count and has little power.

6. Updated beliefs (INFERENCE)
These are absolute levels, not calibrated deltas: the full h-001/h-002/h-003 texts were not re-read this session because the ledger output was too large.
- h-001 (structure adds value): 0.25 -> 0.20. Second null; recall and AUC deltas disagree in sign again.
- h-002 (UCB kappa=2 exploration beats RF+EI at the practical margin): 0.35 -> 0.25. Two runs put the effect at about +0.03. The 95% upper bound of 0.0608 still allows a margin-sized effect, but most of the CI mass lies below 0.05.
- h-003 (fixed RF+EI is sufficient / practically equivalent): 0.55 -> 0.50. Part (i) holds strongly, but formal equivalence just failed, and the direction favours C in both runs.
- Uncertainty is high. The best current estimate is a small positive C-B effect of about +0.03 recall (roughly 2 of 63 targets per seed) whose sign is not established at 95%.

prereg-003 is an exact second block of prereg-002, run within the override limits:
- budget 100, n_seeds 30 (the maximum), seed_offset 200 (seeds 200-229, disjoint from 0-9 and 100-129);

Also preregister:
- a stratified secondary on initial top hits (0 vs 1 or more), to test surprise (c);
- the tie rule must be reported.
Not chosen: budget 200, because the ceiling there is known (B 0.956).

8. Validation still needed before real-world use
This is still a retrospective, noiseless replay of precomputed DFPT labels on a cleaned pool (1265 of 1521). Before real-world use the lab still needs:
- a prospective or held-out-pool test with real calculation cost and failures;
- a calibration check of RF uncertainty in the top tail;
- a duplicate-polymorph leakage check;
- a shuffled-structure control and a declared max_features;
- replication on a second phonon dataset.
Nothing here licenses "agent design is superior" or "agent design is unnecessary".

MAIN LIMITATION: the primary contrast is underpowered for an effect of about 0.03 given the large seed heterogeneity. The verdict is inconclusive, not null.

label: EVIDENCE
text: Petretto et al. (2018, Sci. Data) used density functional perturbation theory in the harmonic approximation to compute full phonon dispersions and vibrational DOS for 1521 semiconductor compounds, with derived dielectric and thermodynamic properties. They validated the results against experimental data. This is the database behind the 1521-material pool, of which 1265 remain after cleaning.

label: EVIDENCE
text: In an ML study of Debye temperature across 495 high-entropy carbides (XGBoost, 19 compositional descriptors, targets from Anderson's model, not DFPT), the model reached R2 = 0.96. Lower atomic masses drove higher Debye temperature, which correlated strongly with average atomic number (rho = -0.92). Scope: one materials family, a model-derived target, and Debye temperature rather than the last DOS peak.

label: EVIDENCE
text: Choudhary et al. (2020, npj Comput. Mater.) computed Gamma-point phonons with high-throughput DFPT for 5015 non-metallic JARVIS-DFT materials. They analysed chemistry, symmetry, dimensionality and geometry as features explaining variation in the data, and built high-accuracy regression models for the highest infrared frequency. The abstract does not say how much composition contributes compared with structure.

label: EVIDENCE
text: Structure-aware models can predict the phonon DOS directly. Euclidean neural networks that take atomic species and positions as input, and are equivariant to crystal symmetry, predicted phonon DOS well from a small training set (Chen et al., 2021). The graph-attention Mat2Spec model outperformed the prior state of the art for ab initio phDOS prediction (Kong et al., 2022). Neither abstract reports a composition-only ablation.

label: EVIDENCE
text: Liang et al. (2021, npj Comput. Mater.) benchmarked Bayesian optimization across five experimental materials systems. Random-forest surrogates performed comparably to anisotropic-kernel GPs, and both outperformed isotropic-kernel GPs. RF needs less initial hyperparameter selection and makes no distribution assumptions. A 2026 benchmark that used uniform random search as the control likewise found RF (Lolopy) matching or exceeding GP performance in some settings.

label: EVIDENCE
text: Sequential-learning gains depend on the goal and on the setup. Rohr et al. (2020) benchmarked SL against separate goals: finding any good material, finding all good materials, and finding an accurate model. Borg et al. (2023) showed that traditional model error metrics are decoupled from how well a model guides discovery. A multi-fidelity SL study reports that agent performance depends on data size, model choice and acquisition strategy.

label: EVIDENCE
text: Known failure modes. Conventional BO can be inefficient in large discrete candidate spaces, evaluating low-value regions before reaching informative ones (arXiv 2608.04651). Cold-start active learning, with no initial labels, has been addressed by coverage-aware methods that encourage early diversity (arXiv 2509.25376). Diversity terms are also used to reduce sampling redundancy in uncertainty-based AL (IEEE Access 2022). The last two are not materials studies.

label: UNCERTAINTY
text:
What the retrieved literature does NOT establish:
(1) No source quantifies the predictors of the LAST phonon DOS peak on the Petretto pool. The light-mass link (ev-102) comes from Debye temperature in carbides. Bond stiffness came up only qualitatively, in unrelated systems such as vacancy-induced DOS stiffening.
(2) No source runs a composition-only vs structure-aware ablation for phonon frequencies. Structure-aware DOS models (ev-104) were not compared with composition baselines in their abstracts.
(3) No source benchmarks UCB vs EI with RF surrogates for a top-k recall objective on a phonon dataset, or under a budget of about 100-200 calls.
(4) Evidence on cold start and low diversity (ev-107) is mostly from outside materials, and nothing shows how often these failures hurt RF+EI on small, clustered chemistries.
(5) Nothing addresses calibration of RF uncertainty in the top tail, leakage between polymorphs or duplicates, or seed-to-seed variance of top-k recall in retrospective replays.
(6) Abstract excerpts only; full texts were not inspected.

label: INFERENCE
text:
Interpretation only, not sourced:
(a) The mass link (ev-102) suggests that composition descriptors encoding light elements, such as mean or minimum atomic mass, carry much of the signal for high last-peak frequency. That would be consistent with the small, non-significant structure benefit recorded in dec-001 and dec-002.
(b) The finding that RF and GP perform comparably (ev-105) supports RF+EI as a reasonable, strong baseline. Small gains from changing the acquisition function, such as about +0.03 for UCB, are therefore plausible.
(c) Because evaluation is goal-dependent (ev-106), top-k recall should stay the preregistered primary metric rather than model error.

text:
CRITIQUE of h-004 (structure adds 0 to +0.03 recall over composition in RF+EI). Critic inference, not a result.

1. The support rule cannot be met at the predicted effect size. dec-002's delta_s 95% CI [-0.0206, +0.0561] at n=30 implies a per-seed SD of about 0.103. At n=60 the 90% CI half-width is about 0.022. For the 90% CI to sit inside +/-0.03, the pooled mean must be at most about 0.008. The hypothesis predicts a mean between 0 and 0.03, and the best estimate so far is +0.016. At that value the 90% upper bound is about 0.038, so TOST fails. h-004 is therefore built to come out "inconclusive" in most of its own predicted range. There is also a large dead zone: a mean of 0.008 to 0.03, or a mean of 0.03 or more without LB > 0 or without 2/3 wins, neither supports nor contradicts the hypothesis. That makes it close to unfalsifiable.

2. It double-dips on seeds. Seeds 100-129 produced the +0.016 that motivated h-004, and they are half of the pooled 60. A pooled confirmatory test that reuses the generating data is not a test.

3. Construct validity. The 4 "structure" features (density, vpa, packing fraction, n_sites) are not what drives the highest phonon frequencies. Bond stiffness, coordination, nearest-neighbour bond length and bonding topology are absent. Density and vpa are also largely predictable from composition: Magpie mean atomic volume and mass features already approximate them. A null here says only that these 4 redundant global scalars add little. It does NOT answer the secondary research question, "does crystal structure add signal?" Any write-up must scope the claim this way.

4. Dilution and implementation. Structure is 4 of 127 columns and RF max_features is undeclared. With max_features='sqrt' (about 11 per split), a given structure column is a candidate at only about 8.7% of splits. With 1.0 (the sklearn default in recent versions), dilution matters little. Without knowing which, the sign of any null cannot be interpreted.

5. Polymorph leakage and censoring. Composition-only features cannot tell polymorphs apart, so same-formula entries share one prediction. If top-5% materials cluster in polymorph or duplicate-composition groups, the composition arm gets "free" siblings once one is found, or wastes calls on low-frequency siblings. Either effect moves delta_s by 1/63 = 0.016 per material, the same size as the whole effect. Separately, removing 256 unstable entries (1521 -> 1265) removes exactly the cases where structure (dynamical stability) is most informative. The censored pool is biased against structure.

6. Scope. The ablation exists only under EI. A null in B says nothing about structure under UCB (C), which is the arm the lab might deploy.

7. Chemical-family mode collapse. Both arms may converge on the same light-element families (B, C, N, O, H-rich, Be, Li). If they do, delta_s measures nothing about structure, only which family the first hit came from.

FALSIFICATION CRITERION (h-004 is wrong if any holds):
(i) On fresh block 2 alone (seeds 200-229): delta_s 95% LB > 0 and mean >= 0.03.
(ii) Real minus shuffled-structure recall has 95% LB > 0 and mean >= 0.03, whether pooled or in block 2.
(iii) 95% UB of delta_s < 0, meaning structure hurts.
Plain non-support: with an estimate near 0.016, failing TOST at +/-0.03 is the expected outcome and must be reported as INCONCLUSIVE, not as support.

REQUIRED CONTROLS:
(a) A shuffled-structure arm: permute the 4 structure columns across materials, with a fixed permutation per seed.
(b) A declared max_features, plus a sensitivity run with structure-only and with structure up-weighted (for example, forced into the candidate set).
(c) A polymorph audit: count duplicate reduced formulas in the pool and in the top 63, and report recall with grouped (formula-level) counting.
(d) Report the top-set tie rule.
(e) An offline diagnostic, outside the oracle budget and labelled as non-campaign: 5-fold CV Spearman correlation and top-63 precision with and without structure on the full labelled pool.

FAIR DECISION RULE: Block 2 is the confirmatory test at alpha 0.05. The pooled 60-seed analysis is secondary and labelled as reusing the hypothesis-generating data. Apply Holm across the 3 primary contrasts (C-B, delta_s, B-A). Any claim about "crystal structure" in general is out of scope.

1. The pooled test is double-dipped and runs as a sequential design without alpha spending. Block 1 gave C-B = +0.0296 with 95% CI [-0.004, 0.061], which implies a per-seed SD of about 0.087. Block 2 was added BECAUSE block 1 was inconclusive. At n=60 the pooled 95% half-width is about 0.0225, so h-005's "sign established" needs a pooled mean > 0.0225. That means a block-2 mean of only about 0.0155 or more. A block-2 mean of 0.016 has its own 95% CI of roughly [-0.016, +0.048], with no evidence on its own, yet it would "confirm" h-005 by leaning on the seeds that generated it. Nominal 95% is not valid here. This is the single most important flaw.

2. The "replication" is overstated. +0.0317 (dec-001) came from budget 200, 10 seeds, near the ceiling (B 0.956). That is a different estimand, so it does not independently replicate +0.0296 at budget 100. In dec-001 the early-speed signals did not hold up either (AUC +0.0327 -> +0.0055; calls-to-50% ratio 1.11 -> 1.0).

3. Granularity. One target is 1/63 = 0.0159 recall. The predicted range of +0.015 to +0.045 is 1 to 3 materials per seed. One polymorph duplicate, a tie-rule choice, or one censored entry per seed shifts the verdict.

4. The mechanism is asserted, not measured. Nothing logs whether EI "over-samples low-value regions" or whether UCB "reaches more of the tail". There is also a cheaper rival explanation: an untuned EI baseline. If the EI xi, the incumbent definition, or the RF-variance estimator is weak, EI can collapse into near-greedy behaviour or stall. Then C wins against a strawman, not because uncertainty helps. kappa=2 was kept after the agent saw the results, while EI got no equivalent tuning. That is an asymmetric tuning budget.

5. RF uncertainty is a heuristic. Tree-ensemble variance is unreliable in small-data regimes (arXiv 2603.12567) and is uncalibrated in the top tail (ev-gaps-2 item 5). At 20 to 120 labels, "UCB kappa=2" may be greedy plus structured noise. A greedy (kappa=0) arm and a greedy-plus-random-jitter arm are needed to show that the *uncertainty* term, not perturbation, causes the gain.

6. Pool censoring flatters exploration. Unstable entries (256 removed) never cost an oracle call here. In a real campaign, exploration-heavy acquisition is more likely to hit dynamically unstable or failed calculations, which burn budget and return no label. The retrospective benefit of UCB is an upper bound.

7. Chemical-family mode collapse. UCB could raise recall by hammering one light-element family that happens to hold many of the 63 targets. That is a recall gain without broader discovery. Family-level recall (targets found per chemical family, per anion group) must be reported. The current diversity proxy tracks hit count (dec-002 5d) and has no power.

8. Cold-start subgroup claim. The stratified secondary (>=1 vs 0 initial hits) had n=9 in the 0-hit arm and its sign reversed between runs. Reporting two subgroup means is not a test. It needs an interaction estimate with a CI, labelled exploratory.

9. Internal inconsistency. The support rule ("95% LB > 0 and mean < 0.05") accepts means of 0.045 to 0.05 that fall outside the predicted magnitude. "Contradicted" needs mean < 0.01, which leaves [0.01, 0.0225) as a dead zone.

FALSIFICATION CRITERION (h-005 is wrong if any holds):
(i) Block 2 alone (fresh seeds 200-229): mean <= 0, or 95% UB < +0.015 (the effect is smaller than the predicted floor).
(ii) Pooled 60 with alpha-spending (Pocock, 0.0294 per look, or O'Brien-Fleming): LB <= 0.
(iii) A kappa=0 greedy arm or a tuned-EI arm comes within 0.01 of C. The uncertainty-acquisition mechanism is then refuted, even if C > B.
(iv) Pooled mean > 0.045: refutes the magnitude claim, in the other direction.

REQUIRED CONTROLS:
- Matched initial sets: the per-arm hash check must pass for block 2 as well.
- Fresh seeds only for confirmation. If any decision follows block 2, confirm it on seeds 300+.
- A greedy arm (kappa=0).
- A tuned-EI arm (xi grid chosen on seeds 0-9 only, as C was).
- Mechanism logs per batch: mean predicted mu and sigma of picks, the fraction of picks in the current top-predicted 5%, and the number of distinct families.
- Family-level recall.
- A tie rule.
- A budget curve (40/70/100 calls) from the same runs, to show the effect is not one cherry-picked operating point.

FAIR DECISION RULE: Block 2 is the confirmatory test at alpha 0.05. The pooled analysis is reported with alpha-spending and disclosed as reusing the generating data. Holm across the primaries.

text:
CRITIQUE of h-006 (null: C-B within +/-0.05; B >= 2x random; RF+EI practically sufficient). Critic inference.

1. h-005 and h-006 overlap, so the ledger can "confirm" both. At n=60 (SD about 0.087), the 95% half-width is about 0.0225 and the 90% half-width about 0.0188. h-005 is supported if the pooled mean > 0.0225. h-006 TOST passes if |pooled mean| < 0.0312. Any pooled mean in (0.0225, 0.0312) supports both. With block 1 fixed at +0.0296, that corresponds to a block-2 mean between about 0.0155 and 0.0328, which is exactly where the current estimate sits. The run cannot discriminate between these two hypotheses near the most likely outcome. h-006 is also a coin-flip on noise: block-1 + 0.0296 is only 0.0016 below its own TOST cliff.

2. The universal claim is untested. "No agent-chosen variant within the spec space beats RF+EI by >= 0.05" is tested with ONE variant (C). Passing TOST for C says nothing about the other feature_set x acquisition x kappa x diversity cells. Either restrict the claim to C, or test the space with multiplicity correction and a held-out confirmation, accepting the winner's curse.

3. The margin is unjustified. 0.05 was fixed when headroom was expected at about 0.5. Realised headroom is 0.309, so the margin is 16% of it (dec-002 5a). 0.05 is about 3 of 63 targets. "Practically sufficient" is a cost claim stated in recall units with no cost model. The margin should be justified in oracle calls, as equivalent-recall call savings with a CI, before the run. It must not be changed afterwards.

4. The control criterion has no teeth. "B >= 2x random" was already passed at 7.6x (0.691 vs 0.091). It cannot fail and so tests nothing. The real threat to "the BO pipeline is sufficient" is that NO learning is needed. Add a zero-oracle-learning heuristic arm, D_prior: rank by a physics prior (for example ascending Magpie mean or minimum atomic mass, per ev-102) and take the top 120. If D_prior is within 0.05 of B, then "BO is sufficient" is the wrong framing: domain knowledge is sufficient and the BO pipeline adds little.

5. The secondary criterion is ill-posed. The calls-to-50% ratio of 0.9-1.1 is set at batch granularity. The median is about 90 calls with batch 10, so one batch gives 80/90 = 0.889 or 100/90 = 1.111, and the criterion fails on a single-batch difference. Use the paired recall-curve AUC or interpolated calls-to-50% with a CI.

6. Shared flaws with h-005: seeds 100-129 are reused (pooled support is partly postdiction), and there is no alpha-spending for the two-stage design.

7. Failure modes:
- Retrospective oracle: noiseless, precomputed DFPT, so "sufficiency" ignores calculation failures and cost heterogeneity.
- Pool censoring: 1265 of 1521. RF+EI sufficiency on a pre-cleaned pool says nothing about pools containing unstable structures.
- Cold start: with 20 random labels, about 1 initial hit on average (9/30 seeds had 0). B's sufficiency may hold only on average while failing badly on 0-hit seeds. Report the lower-tail per-seed recall (10th percentile) and the worst seed, not only the mean.
- Mode collapse: B may reach 0.69 by mining one light-element family. Report family-level recall.
- Seed variance: the per-seed range is -0.19 to +0.21, so mean equivalence can hide large per-seed risk.

8. Research-question confound. B and C differ ONLY in acquisition (same composition_structure features). The primary RQ asks about an "evidence-informed, agent-designed campaign", but this run tests UCB vs EI. Neither h-006 support nor h-005 support licenses any statement about agent DESIGN. That needs a null-agent control: a spec drawn uniformly at random from the allowed space, evaluated on the same seeds. If agent-chosen C does not beat randomly-chosen specs, the "evidence-informed" part adds nothing.

FALSIFICATION CRITERION (h-006 is wrong if any holds):
(i) Block-2 or pooled (alpha-spent) C-B 95% LB > 0 and mean >= 0.05.
(ii) Any preregistered alternative spec beats B by >= 0.05 with Holm-adjusted LB > 0, confirmed on fresh seeds.
(iii) D_prior (no learning) within 0.05 of B. This refutes "the BO pipeline is what matters" without refuting equivalence.
(iv) B's 10th-percentile per-seed recall < 2x random mean. This refutes practical sufficiency in the cold-start tail.

FAIR, MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE DECISION TABLE, preregistered on block 2 (confirmatory). Pooled is secondary and alpha-spent:
- R1: 95% LB > 0 and mean >= 0.05 -> C practically superior (h-006 falsified, h-005 magnitude falsified).
- R2: 95% LB > 0 and 90% UB < 0.05 -> real but sub-margin (h-005 supported; h-006 supported only for C).
- R3: 95% LB > 0, 90% UB >= 0.05, mean < 0.05 -> sign established, practical status unresolved.
- R4: 95% LB <= 0 and 90% CI inside +/-0.05 -> equivalent (h-006 supported for C; h-005 not supported).
- R5: 95% UB < 0 -> C worse.
- R6: otherwise INCONCLUSIVE, which is not evidence for the null.
Exactly one row fires. Holm across C-B, delta_s and B-vs-D_prior. Restate the margin in calls before the run.

PREREGISTRATION prereg-003 (chosen design d-005; rejected d-006). STATUS: PROPOSED, NOT APPROVED. Only a human may approve it, outside this session. Nothing has been run.

SPEC. Arms (all on identical protocol and hash-matched initial sets):
- A_random: composition_structure, random.
- B_baseline_ei: composition_structure, RF + EI.
- B_ablation_composition_only: composition, RF + EI.
- C_crucible: composition_structure, RF + UCB, kappa=2.0, diversity=none. Unchanged from prereg-002, so the seed block is the only thing that changes.
Surrogate: random forest, 100 trees (max_features is not exposed by the tooling; the runner must report the value used).
Protocol: initial_size 20; batch 10; budget 100, so 120 oracle calls per seed including the initial 20; top_fraction 0.05 (n_top 63); n_seeds 30; seed_offset 200, i.e. seeds 200-229, never used before. Seeds 0-9 and 100-129 are already spent.
Cost: 14,400 simulated oracle calls.

CONFIRMATORY SCOPE. Block 2 (seeds 200-229) alone is confirmatory. The pooled 60-seed analysis (100-129 plus 200-229) is SECONDARY, uses Pocock alpha spending (0.0294 per look, two-sided), and is disclosed as reusing the hypothesis-generating seeds. It cannot overturn a block-2 row.
Multiplicity: Holm across the 3 primary contrasts: C-B, delta_s (B_baseline_ei minus B_ablation_composition_only), and B-A.
Statistics: paired seed-level bootstrap, 10,000 resamples, percentile CIs, fixed bootstrap seed.
- 'LB>0' / 'UB<0' means the Holm-adjusted two-sided p < 0.05, in that direction.
- Equivalence (TOST) uses the unadjusted 90% CI.

MARGIN, derived from ledger numbers only (result-prereg-002 and dec-002):
- At 120 calls, B reached 0.691, so headroom was 0.309, and B's median calls to 50% recall was 90.
- B's end-of-campaign slope is about (0.691 - 0.50)/30 calls, or roughly 0.0064 recall per call. This mixes a mean and a median, so it is approximate.
- C-B practical margin is kept at 0.05 so the goalposts do not move. That is 3.2 of 63 targets, 16% of headroom, and about 8 oracle calls (≈1 batch, 6.5% of the 120-call budget) of B's late-campaign yield.
- Structure margin is 0.03: about 1.9 targets, or about 5 calls.

POWER. dec-002 implies a per-seed SD of about 0.087. Block 2 alone therefore has a 95% half-width of about 0.033 and a 90% half-width of about 0.027. A true effect of +0.03 gives roughly a 40-50% chance that LB>0. An INCONCLUSIVE result is likely, and it is not evidence for the null.

OUTCOME TABLE, C-B on block 2. Rules are evaluated in order and exactly one row fires:
- R0, protocol failure: pairing_check is not verified -> no inference.
- R5, C worse: UB<0.
- R1, C practically superior: LB>0 AND mean >= 0.05 AND C wins >= 2/3 of non-tied seeds.
- R2, real but sub-margin: LB>0 AND 90% UB < 0.05.
- R3, sign only: LB>0, and neither R1 nor R2.
- R4, equivalent: 90% CI inside (-0.05, +0.05).
- R6, INCONCLUSIVE: anything else.

STRUCTURE TABLE, delta_s on block 2, scoped to the 4 scalar structure features only:
- S0 (R0 fired): no inference.
- S1, structure hurts: UB<0.
- S2, structure helps: LB>0 AND mean >= 0.03.
- S3, small real gain: LB>0 AND mean < 0.03.
- S4, no meaningful benefit: 90% CI inside ±0.03.
- S5: inconclusive.
